scene_actors:
Scene actor lists (bank $0C in the extraction = ROM bank $8C, 819200-845284): the spawn script of every scene. scene_actors is a 256-entry table of word pointers indexed by scene id; each pointer leads to one scene record = actor list + $FF terminator + title string. SpawnSceneActors (actor_execution) walks the list when a scene loads and leaves $3E on the terminator; DisplaySceneTitle (called right after it, scene_lifecycle) reads the title string that follows.

=== ROM LAYOUT vs EXTRACTION ===

The ROM holds the 512-byte pointer table (819200-819711) and then 241 scene records back to back. Each record is the list, the $FF that ends it and the title string ended by $CA. The extraction cuts every title out of its record (post-process Extract(1)): the list stays as scene_NN_actors [ ... ] (NN = the scene id in hex) and the title becomes scene_NN_actors_value, with a second pointer table scene_actors_extract_table at the end of the file. scene_actors_extract_table is generated by the extractor (a copy of the pointer table that points at the titles) and has no bytes of its own; in the ROM the first title byte is the byte right after the list's $FF. The record shared by the 16 unused ids is scene_default_actors (the first record in the ROM, 819712).

=== RECORD FORMAT (actor list) ===

Records of two kinds follow each other until a hidden $FF:
- actor-spawn, 7 bytes: tile X, tile Y, attribute byte, long pointer to an actor-def, and a hidden stats byte $00 (the discriminator; the extraction hides it).
- enemy-spawn, 9 bytes: the same first six bytes, then stats table index (nonzero, the discriminator), enemy number and event-block index.
InitActorFromSceneData reads them: tile X/Y x 16 = pixel position ($14/$16). Attribute byte, bit 0 clear: ((byte & $F6) << 8) | word at $06F0 goes into $0E (oamXorFlags; sprite_composition XORs it into the tile / attribute word of every sub-sprite, so $30 = OAM priority 3 and $02 = the lowest palette bit; for the player, bit $02 of the byte becomes the combat lock and is cleared from $0E); bit 0 set: byte >> 1 is a spawn parameter (3 = parameter 1, $0B = 5, $21 = $10). Enemy number nonzero: CheckEnemyDefeatedFlag tests bit (number AND 7) of wramFlags byte number / 8 ($0A80..); a set bit skips the record, frees the slot and optionally swaps the event block. Stats index nonzero: the actor counts in enemiesRemaining and takes its HP from the enemy stats table.

=== WHOLE-FILE COUNTS ===

- 256 table entries -> 241 records: 240 scenes have their own record, and 16 unused scene ids ($48 $57 $76 $77 $80 $81 $9E $AA $AB $AF $C1 $C2 $CA $CB $F8 $F9) share the default record scene_default_actors (player, camera controller, ScrollCameraTrack; title TEST MAP). No scene-warp destination and no QueueMapChange operand names any of those ids.
- 1,798 actor-spawn + 1,317 enemy-spawn = 3,115 spawn records. Longest lists: scene_A7_actors (scene $A7, 62 records, many ramps and speed zones) and scene_91_actors (scene $91 Euro, 58).
- Enemy records: stats index $01-$63 (62 distinct values); enemy numbers $00-$FE (254 distinct, 70 records use 0 = no defeat tracking); 42 records name an event block.
- Titles: 241 strings, 64 non-empty (the town, house, dungeon and area names such as South Cape, Itory Village, Diamond Mine, Sky Garden, Mu, Pyramid, six Dark Space rooms, Demon Palace). The other 177 are the single byte $CA (count 0, DisplaySceneTitle shows nothing). Several rooms of one area carry the same title.

=== CONVENTIONS IN THE DATA ===

- 224 lists (the 223 scene lists that begin with a player, plus scene_default_actors) start with player_character.PlayerCharacterDef as record $00. This is what makes SpawnSceneActors' playerActorDp = $1000 (first actor slot) true. Player attribute byte: $00 / $30 combat scenes, $02 / $32 non-combat scenes (88 and 6 uses): bit $02 sets the combat lock, bit $30 the priority (see InitActorFromSceneData).
- 220 lists carry camera_scroll_controller, always as record $01 except in scene $89 (record $00, no player). The camera mode actor follows in most scenes (ScrollCameraTrack, ScrollCameraVertical, ScrollCameraInit or ScrollCameraAccumulate; a few scenes use layer1_scroll_actors instead).
- 17 lists do not start with the player (241 records - 224): $00 and $9F are empty (only $FF + $CA); $59 garden_crash_cutscene, $89 camera + s89_new_babel, $8C / $8D / $8F pr8C-pr8F prologue scenes, $90 s90_changed_world, $C0 future_vision_cutscene, $F0 sF0_class_dismissed, $F7 credits (sF7_credits_player and five credits NPCs), $FA diary menu, $FB boot logo, $FC title intro, $FD statue_inventory_reward, $FE WorldMapController, $FF inventory menu.
scene_thinkers:
Per-scene thinker spawn lists (Bank 0C, 845285-846683 = $0C:E5E5): a 256-word pointer table indexed by scene ID x 2 ($0646), followed by 70 lists of thinker-spawn records (204 records in all). SpawnSceneThinkers (thinker_execution) runs once per scene build: it reads scene_thinkers[$0646], allocates a thinker slot for every record up to the $FF terminator and calls InitThinkerFromSceneData. A zero pointer or a first byte with bit 7 set means no thinkers. The old note ('background AI thinkers: palette cyclers, HDMA effects, ambient handlers') was only half right: global_ambient_dispatcher, which 59 of the 70 lists contain, is the player palette and the talk interaction, not an ambient effect.

=== RECORD (4 bytes, extraction: thinker-spawn < param, @code >) ===

| Byte | Field |
|------|-------|
| +0 | Spawn parameter: stored as animScratch+2 ($7F0002,X) of the new thinker. What it means is up to the code: the palette bundle ID for ambient_palette_cycler, the parallax_scroll_table index ($00-$24) for scanline_band_hdma_thinker, unused ($00) for most others |
| +1..+3 | Long pointer to the thinker's code; its first word becomes the thinker's filter flags (animScratch2) and the entry point is code + 2 |

A list ends with a $FF byte (bit 7 of byte 0 is the test), which the extraction does not print.

=== SHARING ===

- 70 of the 256 scenes use the bare list thinker_spawn_dispatcher_only (only global_ambient_dispatcher). Three more lists hold the same single record (0CE8E1 for scene $40, 0CE8EF and 0CE8F4 for scenes $4B and $4C).
- 43 scenes point at thinker_spawn_0CE7EA+8: the table entry may point into the middle of another scene's list, so a scene starts at a later record. The offset is in hex and counts bytes (4 per record): +4 skips one record, +8 two. 0CE7EA holds ambient_palette_cycler ($3F), flag_gated_palette_cool, scanline_band_hdma_thinker ($02) and global_ambient_dispatcher, so +8 = scanline band $02 plus the dispatcher. Two scenes ($04, $07) enter it at +0 and 4 at +4. The other shifted entries: 0CE80C+4, 0CE843+4 (2), 0CE861+8 (4), 0CE87F+4, 0CE8A1+8, 0CE96F+8 (2), 0CE9E1+4 (8), 0CEA11+4 (6).
- 67 of the 70 lists are reached from the table. Unreferenced: 0CE8E6 (scanline band $20 + dispatcher), 0CE9EA (palette bundles $01 and $32, dispatcher, scanline band $0F) and 0CEA45 (bundles $44 and $45 + dispatcher, a copy of 0CEA2F).
- The dispatcher is the last record in most lists but the first in some (for example 0CE8C7, 0CE959, 0CE98D, 0CE99A, 0CE9A3, 0CE9AC); the credits list 0CEA5B has none.

=== WHAT THE CODE FILES SAY ===

The block notes of ambient_palette_cycler, scanline_band_hdma_thinker and global_ambient_dispatcher describe the parameters. The 204 records are 59 ambient_palette_cycler, 59 global_ambient_dispatcher, 30 scanline_band_hdma_thinker and 56 spread over the other thinker code files. The list order is the spawn order. What each bundle or band looks like on screen was not traced.

Byte check: 1398 = 512 (256 pointers) + 204 x 4 (records) + 70 ($FF terminators). The ?INCLUDE list at the top names the 45 thinker code files the records point at.
sE7_space_bg_scroll:
Space background parallax scroll for the space flight.

Manages the scrolling starfield background during
the approach to the comet. Multi-layer parallax
for depth effect in space.
sE7_space_flight_controller:
Space flight sequence controller (~212 lines).

Controls the Mode 7-style space flight sequence as Will
travels from the Tower of Babel to the comet. Manages
sprite scaling, camera movement, star particle spawning,
and the dramatic approach to the comet's surface.
sE8_comet_display_config:
Comet lair display configuration (~132 lines).

Initializes the full display setup for the Dark Gaia boss
arena: palette loading, HDMA channel configuration, BG
layer priorities, and the cosmic background starfield.
Must execute before the boss fight begins.
sE8_dark_gaia:
Dark Gaia — the final boss of the game (~1,005 lines).

Multi-form final boss with the game's largest boss script.
Phase 1: Dark Gaia's face attacks with energy beams and
summoned projectiles. Phase 2: transformation into the
comet form with new attack patterns. Phase 3: final
desperate assault. Uses extensive camera control, palette
manipulation, and spawned child actors for attacks.
Defeat triggers the ending sequence.
